Although transient abnormalities in liver function commonly occur during the early stages of antitubercu- losis treatment, drugs other than ethambutol are generally con- sidered responsible. Ethambutol has generated fewer reports of hepatotoxicity to the UK CSM than rifampicin, isoniazid, or pyrazinamide,1 and the use of regimens containing ethambutol has been recommended for patients unable to tolerate standard regimens due to hepatotoxicity.1-3 1. Ormerod LP, et al. Hepatotoxicity of antituberculosis drugs. Thorax 1996; 51: 111–13. 2. Joint Tuberculosis Committee of the British Thoracic Society.
